entries.title: Genesis 47:4
segments:
Sore; very grievous. 
 
Notwithstanding our dependence on God for all the blessings we enjoy and hope for, it is as needful to use all suitable means to obtain these blessings, as it would be if success depended solely on our efforts.  Compare

entries.title: Genesis 47:9
segments:
Pilgrimage; journey through this world. 
 
The longest life is but a journey through this world to another; and as character is the chief thing, our great concern should be that it may be such as shall render us most useful and fit us for heaven.

entries.title: Genesis 47:11
segments: Rameses; the capital of Goshen, about half way from the Nile to the Red sea.

entries.title: Genesis 47:20
segments: Men will cheerfully give up their property to save the life of the body; and yet, for the sake of property, they will sacrifice the life of their souls.

entries.title: Genesis 47:21
segments: Removed them to cities; where the food was stored, for the greater convenience of supplying them.

entries.title: Genesis 47:22
segments: Priests; the priests of Egypt were a very powerful and influential body, and enjoyed many privileges above the common people.

entries.title: Genesis 47:23
segments: Sow the land; as the seven years of famine were now drawing to a close.

entries.title: Genesis 47:25
segments: To be ungrateful to one who has saved our life, would be base; how much more so not to be grateful to Him who, by suffering and death for us, has opened a way to save the undying soul.

entries.title: Genesis 47:26
segments: The fifth part; this is supposed to have been the tax which they paid for the use of the land and the support of the government.

entries.title: Genesis 47:30
segments:
This Jacob did, not merely because he wished to be buried by the side of his fathers, but also as an expression of his faith in the promise of God that his posterity should inherit that land. 
 
The pious at death wish to have such disposal made of their bodies as shall be most useful to survivors, and, if consistent, to have them laid with the bodies of pious ancestors; that at the trump of the archangel they may rise and ascend together, and complete in body and soul, be ever with the Lord.

entries.title: Genesis 47:31
segments: , the Septuagint, or Greek translation, is followed: worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.
